How expiring, pending delete and dropped domains work, and how to get one when it is released. What are expired domains? An expired domain is a name whose owner did not renew it by its domain expiration date. It is not free yet: the owner usually still has a grace period and a redemption period. Only when the registry deletes it, when the domain drops, can anyone register it. What does pending delete mean? Pending delete is the last stage before a domain is deleted, usually five days for .com and .net. Nobody can renew the name any more. ScopeFlux lists pending delete and deleted domains with the day they are expected to drop. How can I buy an expired domain? Wait for the release day and register the name at any registrar, or place a backorder with a drop catching service before it drops. Popular names are often caught within seconds. ScopeFlux does not sell or register domains; it shows when a name is expected to become available. When does a domain expire, and when is it released? Use the domain expiration checker to see a domain’s expiration date from public registry data. For listed names, ScopeFlux shows the estimated release day from the source: Verisign pending-delete lists for .com and .net, the registries’ own drop lists for .it and .au, Backorder.sk for .sk and CZ.NIC for .cz. Which extensions are covered? .com, .net, .org, .io, .app, .xyz, .info, .me, .biz, .us, .pro, .cc, .tv, .co.uk, .uk, .org.uk, .com.au, .au, .it, .sk and .cz. Expiring .sk and .cz domains are rarely covered by other expired domain lists. Is the expired domains list free? Yes. Browsing, search, filters and the watchlist are free. Signing in with Google is optional and keeps your watchlist on all your devices. CSV export and API access are part of ScopeFlux Premium, a monthly plan. Here is what happens. What happens when an owner forgets to renew: the stages, how long each one lasts and what it costs. THE SHORT VERSION Expired does not mean free. The owner gets extra time to pay, often weeks. Waiting longer costs the owner more. Paying a little late is cheap, paying at the last moment can cost a lot more. Only at the end can anyone else get it. Then it is first come, first served, or an auction. THE TIMELINE From expired to available, step by step. The same order applies to every extension, from stage 1 to stage 5. The exact number of days depends on the registry and the registrar. 01 Active Until the expiration date The domain is registered and paid. Owner Renews at the normal price. Cost Normal renewal 02 Grace period First days or weeks Expired, but the owner can still renew it. The website and email may stop working. Owner Can renew, usually at the normal price. Cost Normal renewal, sometimes a late fee 03 Last chance Before deletion Often called the redemption period: the final stage before the domain is deleted. Only the old owner can still save it. Owner Can still save it, sometimes with an extra restore fee. Cost Renewal or a restore fee 04 Deletion or auction A set day Often called pending delete. Locked: nobody can renew or register it. Then the registry deletes it, or sells it in a public auction. Owner Too late to save it. Cost Not possible 05 Released After deletion or auction The domain is free again. The first registration wins. Owner Anyone can register it. Cost Normal registration or a backorder Owner is safe Owner should pay now Last chance for the owner Locked or auction Free to register It can be sold before it drops Some registrars auction expired names during the grace period, and some registries auction them instead of deleting them. If someone buys it there, the name never becomes free. The release is a race Released names are often caught within seconds by backorder services. If you want a valuable name, be ready on the day or use a backorder. WHAT IT COSTS Fees when an owner forgets to pay. Steps 1 to 5 follow each other in time. This is the general pattern: the details differ by extension (a .cz name, for example, goes to a registry auction), prices are typical, and the registrar’s own price list is what counts. 1 Pays on time Before the expiration date Normal yearly price The usual renewal at the registrar. 2 Pays a little late First days or weeks after expiry Usually still the normal price Some registrars add a small late fee. 3 Pays very late Last stage before deletion Can cost a lot more Some extensions charge a restore fee, often about 50–200 EUR, on top of the renewal. 4 Too late for the owner Deletion or auction Cannot be saved any more The domain is deleted, or sold in an auction. 5 Someone else gets it After release Normal price, a backorder fee or an auction bid Whoever is first registers it at the normal price. A backorder service or an auction can cost more. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR YOU Three things to remember. 01 A date is a forecast Release dates come from public sources. The owner can still renew, so a name can vanish from the list at any time. 02 Timing matters Most good names are taken in the first minutes after release. Know the exact day and be ready, or use a backorder. 03 Check before you plan Open a domain in ScopeFlux to see its current registration status, then confirm with a registrar before you count on it. QUICK ANSWERS Common questions. If a domain is on the list, will it definitely become free? No. The owner can renew it until the last stage, and a registrar may sell it at auction first. A release date is an estimate from the source, not a promise. Can I buy a domain before it is released? Not from the registry. Only the current owner can renew or restore it. Some registrars sell their own expired names at auction during the grace period. Why does the website still work after the expiration date? Many registrars and registries keep the name running for a few days or weeks after expiry, to give the owner a chance to notice and pay. What is a domain backorder or drop catching? A backorder asks a drop catching service to try to register a name the moment it is deleted. If several people backorder the same domain, it usually goes to an auction. ScopeFlux does not place backorders; it shows the expected drop day so you can choose a service in time. Does ScopeFlux register domains? No. ScopeFlux only shows what public sources publish. To register, backorder or bid, use a registrar. Ready to look for a name? Browse the domains that are getting close to release, filtered by your favourite extensions. Extensions: .com, .net, .org, .io, .app, .xyz, .info, .me, .biz, .us, .pro, .cc, .tv, .co.uk, .uk, .org.uk, .com.au, .au, .it, .cz, .sk. GET /api/v1/tlds All extensions with their live source and last update. GET /api/v1/me Your key, plan and usage today. { "data": [{ "domain": "example.com", "tld": "com", "releaseDate": "2026-10-30", "releaseLabel": "Registry deletion day · hour not published", "status": "Expected release", "source": "NameBio", "premiumCandidate": false }], "page": 1, "limit": 100, "hasMore": true } Add format=csv to /domains or /recent for a CSV file. What ScopeFlux stores, who processes it and how to ask for it to be deleted. PRIVACY What ScopeFlux stores, and why. Last updated 28 October 2026. Who runs ScopeFlux ScopeFlux is run by Matúš Šturdík, Nová 407, Veľká Mača, Slovakia, IČO (company ID) 51628163. This is the controller of your personal data. Questions about your data: hello@scopeflux.io . Browsing without an account You can use the catalogue, the history and the domain check without an account. ScopeFlux sets no analytics, advertising or tracking cookies and does not build a profile of you. When you check a domain, the name you typed is sent to public registration services (RDAP registries listed by IANA, and Backorder.sk for .sk details) to read its current status. ScopeFlux does not store which domains you looked up. Visit statistics To see how many people use the site, ScopeFlux uses Cloudflare Web Analytics. It counts page views and visits without cookies, without fingerprinting and without following you across other websites. The figures are only seen in aggregate. Hosting The site and its database are hosted by HostCreators (Slovakia) and delivered through Cloudflare. To deliver pages and protect the site, both process technical request data such as your IP address and browser type, and keep short-lived logs. See Cloudflare’s privacy policy . Watchlist and sign-in You can keep a watchlist without an account: it is then stored only in your browser (local storage) and never sent to ScopeFlux, except to check the names you saved. Signing in is optional. It keeps the watchlist on all your devices. Sign-in is done with your Google account: Google tells ScopeFlux your name, email address and a Google account ID, and ScopeFlux sets one sign-in cookie (sf_session) that is needed for the account to work. ScopeFlux never sees your Google password. To delete your account and everything saved with it, open the account menu and choose Delete account. ScopeFlux stores your account ID, name, email address and the domains you save, with their last checked status, in its database until you remove them. To delete your watchlist, remove the domains or write to hello@scopeflux.io . Premium, API keys and payments For signed-in accounts ScopeFlux stores the plan (Free or Premium). If you create API keys, ScopeFlux stores their names, a one-way hash of each key (never the key itself), when they were last used and how many requests were made per day, to enforce the limits. Usage counts are kept for 90 days. Premium is paid through Stripe. Stripe processes your card and billing details under its privacy policy ; ScopeFlux never sees your card number. ScopeFlux stores only the Stripe customer and subscription IDs, the subscription status and the end of the paid period. Deleting your account cancels an active subscription and removes your keys. E-mail alerts E-mail alerts are off until you switch them on for your watchlist (in the watchlist or the account menu). The legal basis is your consent, which you can withdraw at any time: switch alerts off in the account menu or the watchlist, or use the link at the end of every alert. ScopeFlux then sends no more alerts. Alerts only go to the e-mail address of your Google account, which Google has verified. ScopeFlux stores whether alerts are on, when the last alert was sent, how many deliveries in a row failed (alerts switch off after 3 refused deliveries) and which alerts were already sent (domain, type of alert, date) so you do not get the same alert twice. Sent-alert records are kept for 180 days; deleting your account removes all of these records. The e-mails are sent through the mail server of our hosting provider HostCreators. ScopeFlux does not track opens or clicks and sends no marketing e-mails. Newsletter You can subscribe to the weekly newsletter with any e-mail address, without an account. The legal basis is your consent. ScopeFlux first sends one confirmation e-mail and sends the newsletter only after you confirm with the link in it; an address that is not confirmed within 7 days is deleted. ScopeFlux stores the address, the extensions you chose, when you subscribed and confirmed, and which weekly issue was sent last. Every newsletter has an unsubscribe link (also offered by your mail app as one-click unsubscribe): it deletes the address right away. An address that refuses delivery 3 times in a row is deleted as well. The e-mails are sent from the hosting at HostCreators; ScopeFlux does not track opens or clicks. Your rights Under the GDPR you can ask what data is held about you, and ask for it to be corrected or deleted. Write to hello@scopeflux.io . You can also complain to the Slovak data protection authority (Úrad na ochranu osobných údajov SR). Advertising ScopeFlux shows no advertising today. If that changes, this page will be updated before any ad is shown, and ads will only load after you agree.
